ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached polar plot has the real axis horizontal and the imaginary axis vertical. The plotted locus crosses the negative real axis at approximately -1.42, which is to the left of the critical point -1 + j0. The arrows show the direction of traversal, with the plotted part forming a loop near the upper-left side and a branch extending downward for low frequency. Reasoning: Since the plot crosses at -1.42, the critical point -1 + j0 lies inside the encirclement when the full Nyquist locus is considered. Including the conjugate mirror part required for the complete Nyquist contour, the locus makes two clockwise encirclements of -1 + j0. The open-loop system is stated to be stable, so P = 0. Using the assigned Nyquist count convention, Z = P + N = 0 + 2 = 2. Thus the closed-loop characteristic equation has two right-half-plane zeros, i.e. two closed-loop poles in the right-half s-plane, so the closed-loop system is unstable.
